pr_title: fix(rust, python): get_single_leaf can't handle Expr::Count

issue_context.title: `ComputeError` on `count` on `over` operations on `list` column
issue_context.body:
### Checks

- [X] I have checked that this issue has not already been reported.

- [X] I have confirmed this bug exists on the [latest version](https://pypi.org/project/polars/) of Polars.


### Reproducible example

```python
import polars as pl
(
    pl.DataFrame({
        "a": [["a", "c", "b"], ["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "d", "c"], ["c", "a", "b"]],
        "b": [["a", "c", "b"], ["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "d", "c"], ["c", "a", "b"]]})
    .with_columns(
        pl.count().over(pl.col("a").list.sort().list.join("").hash()).suffix("_cnt"))
)
```


### Issue description

This fails without a descriptive error message:

```
thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: ComputeError(ErrString("unable to find a single leaf column in {expr:?}"))', /Users/runner/work/polars/polars/crates/polars-plan/src/logical_plan/projection.rs:53:51
```

I am aiming to calculate the number of cases where `a` (and `b`) have identical elements, whether or not they are in the same order.

### Expected behavior

Output should be:

```py
(
    pl.DataFrame({
        "a": [["a", "c", "b"], ["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "d", "c"], ["c", "a", "b"]],
        "b": [["a", "c", "b"], ["a", "b", "c"], ["a", "d", "c"], ["c", "a", "b"]]})
    .with_columns(
        pl.Series("a_cnt", [3, 3, 1, 3]))
)
```

comments:
It seems to be the `.suffix()` (also prefix / map_alias) causing the error:
```python
pl.DataFrame({"a": [1]}).select(pl.count().over(True).suffix("c"))
# thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: 
# ComputeError(ErrString("unable to find a single leaf column in {expr:?}"))'
```

**Update:** Simpler repro
```python
pl.select(pl.count().suffix("foo"))
# thread '<unnamed>' panicked at 'called `Result::unwrap()` on an `Err` value: 
# ComputeError(ErrString("unable to find a single leaf column in {expr:?}"))'
```
Ha. I needed that `suffix` because I was performing a similar operation for multiple columns. 😅
IIUC, `pl.count().over(pl.col("a").list.sort().list.join("").hash())` will produce a column named `count` instead of `a`. But yes, `suffix` should work without panicking.

review_comments: Seems that we did not format the error message correctly before
IIUC, `Expr::Count` is a leaf expr, It is different from `AggExpr` which does have an input.
